proposals.before: Zhuangzong’s Empress Jing Shenmin, Lady Liu, came from Cheng’an in Weizhou.
proposals.after: Zhuangzong’s Empress Shenminjing, Lady Liu, came from Cheng’an in Weizhou.
proposals.reason: Chinese posthumous title 神閔敬皇后 should be Shenminjing; Jing Shenmin reverses the title characters.

proposals.before: Zhuangzong’s Empress Jing Shenmin, the Liu clan, was a native of Cheng’an in Weizhou.
proposals.after: Zhuangzong’s Empress Shenminjing, of the Liu clan, was a native of Cheng’an in Weizhou.
proposals.reason: Same posthumous-title reversal as the idiomatic field; 神閔敬 is Shenminjing, not Jing Shenmin.

proposals.before: Lady Han and the others seethed; Han was made Shufei and Yi Defei.
proposals.after: Lady Han and the others seethed; Han was made Shufei and Yi was made Defei.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English fuses Lady Yi with the title Defei as “Yi Defei”; the Chinese separately enfeoffs 伊氏 as 德妃.

proposals.before: Wen Tao of Xuzhou, courting her piety, offered his mansion as a temple for her merit.
proposals.after: Wen Tao of Xu Prefecture, courting her piety, offered his mansion as a temple for her merit.
proposals.reason: Chinese 許州 is Xu Prefecture (around modern Xuchang), not 徐州; “Xuzhou” misidentifies the place.

proposals.before: The military governor of Xuzhou, Wen Tao, because the empress was devoted to Buddhism, asked to make his private residence a monastery to bless her.
proposals.after: The military governor of Xu Prefecture, Wen Tao, because the empress was devoted to Buddhism, asked to make his private residence a monastery to bless her.
proposals.reason: Same 許州 versus 徐州 confusion in the literal English.

proposals.before: In autumn of Tongguang 3 floods ravaged the Yellow River country; refugees clogged the roads, taxes failed, soldiers starved, and next year’s rent was collected early while Zhuangzong and the empress still hunted.
proposals.after: In autumn of Tongguang 3 floods ravaged the two He regions; refugees clogged the roads, taxes failed, soldiers starved, and next year’s rent was collected early while Zhuangzong and the empress still hunted.
proposals.reason: 兩河 denotes the two He regions, not specifically “Yellow River country.”

proposals.before: He left two sons: Sibi and Sigu.
proposals.after: He left two sons: Sibi and Sigong.
proposals.reason: 嗣肱 is Sìgōng; English “Sigu” misreads 肱 (gōng).

proposals.before: Two sons: Sibi and Sigu.
proposals.after: Two sons: Sibi and Sigong.
proposals.reason: 嗣肱 should be romanized Sigong (Sìgōng), not Sigu.

proposals.before: Sigu was bold; under Zhou Dewei he won many fights and became chief adjutant of horse and foot.
proposals.after: Sigong was bold; under Zhou Dewei he won many fights and became chief adjutant of horse and foot.
proposals.reason: Same misromanization of 嗣肱 as Sigu instead of Sigong.

proposals.before: Sigu in youth had daring and strategy; following Zhou Dewei he won many battles and was made chief adjutant of horse and foot.
proposals.after: Sigong in youth had daring and strategy; following Zhou Dewei he won many battles and was made chief adjutant of horse and foot.
proposals.reason: Same misromanization of 嗣肱 as Sigu instead of Sigong.

proposals.before: At Hubi, with Li Cunshen’s victory, Sigu took a Liang general.
proposals.after: At Hubi, with Li Cunshen’s victory, Sigong took a Liang general.
proposals.reason: 嗣肱 should be Sigong, not Sigu.

proposals.before: When Li Cunshen defeated Liang at Hubi, Sigu captured a Liang general.
proposals.after: When Li Cunshen defeated Liang at Hubi, Sigong captured a Liang general.
proposals.reason: 嗣肱 should be Sigong, not Sigu.

proposals.before: When Liang besieged Zhuo, Sigu relieved it with Cunshen; his merit was greatest and he became prefect of Wei and commander north of Yanmen.
proposals.after: When Liang besieged Tiao, Sigong relieved it with Cunshen; his merit was greatest and he became prefect of Yu and commander north of Yanmen.
proposals.reason: 蓚縣 is Tiao, not Zhuo (涿); 嗣肱 is Sigong; 蔚州 is Yu, not Wei.

proposals.before: When Liang’s Taizu besieged Zhuo, Sigu followed Cunshen to relieve it; the Liang army withdrew; Sigu’s merit was greatest; he was promoted to prefect of Wei and commander north of Yanmen.
proposals.after: When Liang’s Taizu besieged Tiao, Sigong followed Cunshen to relieve it; the Liang army withdrew; Sigong’s merit was greatest; he was promoted to prefect of Yu and commander north of Yanmen.
proposals.reason: 蓚縣 misread as Zhuo; 嗣肱 as Sigu; 蔚州 as Wei.

proposals.before: Wang Yu of Xin rebelled to the Khitan; Sigu recovered Ji, Ru, and Wu and became prefect of Xin and commissioner of the northern mountains.
proposals.after: Wang Yu of Xin rebelled to the Khitan; Sigong recovered Ji, Ru, and Wu and became prefect of Xin and commissioner of the northern mountains.
proposals.reason: 嗣肱 should be Sigong, not Sigu.

proposals.before: Wang Yu of Xinzhou rebelled against Jin and fled to the Khitan; the mountain posts all rebelled; Sigu took Ji, Ru, and Wu and was made prefect of Xin and regimental commissioner of the northern mountains.
proposals.after: Wang Yu of Xinzhou rebelled against Jin and fled to the Khitan; the mountain posts all rebelled; Sigong took Ji, Ru, and Wu and was made prefect of Xin and regimental commissioner of the northern mountains.
proposals.reason: 嗣肱 should be Sigong, not Sigu.

proposals.before: From the wars with Helian Duo and Li Keyong through exile among the Tatars and the campaign against Huang Chao, Kening always marched with him.
proposals.after: From the wars with Helian Duo and Li Keju through exile among the Tatars and the campaign against Huang Chao, Kening always marched with him.
proposals.reason: Chinese 李可舉 is Li Keju, not Li Keyong (李克用); the idiomatic English wrongly substitutes Taizu's own name.

proposals.before: When Taizu fought Helian Duo and Li Keyong between Yun and Wei, later fled to the Tatars, entered to break Huang Chao, Kening never failed to follow.
proposals.after: When Taizu fought Helian Duo and Li Keju between Yun and Yu, later fled to the Tatars, entered to break Huang Chao, Kening never failed to follow.
proposals.reason: Chinese 李可舉 must be Li Keju; Li Keyong is a mistranslation of a different person.

proposals.before: Cunmei was Prince of Yong, Cunba Prince of Yong, Cunli Prince of Xue, Cunwo Prince of Shen, Cunyi Prince of Mu, Cunque Prince of Tong, Cunji Prince of Ya.
proposals.after: Cunmei was Prince of Yong (邕), Cunba Prince of Yong (永), Cunli Prince of Xue, Cunwo Prince of Shen, Cunyi Prince of Mu, Cunque Prince of Tong, Cunji Prince of Ya.
proposals.reason: Chinese distinguishes 邕王 (Cunmei) from 永王 (Cunba); both were collapsed to identical 'Prince of Yong'.

proposals.before: Cunmei was Prince of Yong, Cunba Prince of Yong, Cunli Prince of Xue, Cunwo Prince of Shen, Cunyi Prince of Mu, Cunque Prince of Tong, Cunji Prince of Ya.
proposals.after: Cunmei was Prince of Yong (邕), Cunba Prince of Yong (永), Cunli Prince of Xue, Cunwo Prince of Shen, Cunyi Prince of Mu, Cunque Prince of Tong, Cunji Prince of Ya.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise fails to distinguish 邕王 from 永王.

proposals.before: Your merit is great and Father once gave you the realm—I beg you take the command until I can stand alone."
proposals.after: Uncle’s merit and virtue are both high; the late king once entrusted you with government—I dare trouble my younger uncle with the army and government until I can stand on my own."
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits 叔父 and 季父, which identify Kening as Zhuangzong’s younger uncle; the unit’s own literal English already preserves those kinship terms.

proposals.before: He became acting Grand Preceptor and co-equal with the Secretariat.
proposals.after: He became acting Grand Commandant and co-equal with the Secretariat.
proposals.reason: 檢校太尉 is Grand Commandant (太尉), not Grand Preceptor (太師).

proposals.before: He was promoted to acting Grand Preceptor and co-equal with the Secretariat.
proposals.after: He was promoted to acting Grand Commandant and co-equal with the Secretariat.
proposals.reason: 檢校太尉 is Grand Commandant (太尉), not Grand Preceptor (太師).

proposals.before: Jiji told Chongtao: “Father trusts you as Yi Yin and Huo Guang—he will not leave you in the wilds.
proposals.after: Jiji told Chongtao: “His Majesty relies on the Palace Attendant as on Mount Heng and Mount Hua—he will not leave you in the wilds.
proposals.reason: Chinese 陛下 is His Majesty, not Father; 衡、華 are Mount Heng and Mount Hua, not Yi Yin and Huo Guang.

proposals.before: Jiji told Chongtao: “His Majesty relies on you as on Yi Yin and Huo Guang, honors you above the temple, expecting you to pacify all under Heaven and master the four barbarians—surely he will not abandon an elder in barbarian lands.
proposals.after: Jiji told Chongtao: “His Majesty relies on the Palace Attendant as on Mount Heng and Mount Hua, honors you above the temple, expecting you to pacify all under Heaven and master the four barbarians—surely he will not abandon an elder in barbarian lands.
proposals.reason: 衡、華 denote Mount Heng and Mount Hua as metaphors of reliance, not the persons Yi Yin and Huo Guang.

proposals.before: Shu was new; bandits roamed; Chongtao delayed withdrawal while Ren Yuan pacified the hills.
proposals.after: The two Sichuans were newly pacified; Meng Zhixiang had not yet arrived; bandits still gathered in the hills; Chongtao was sending Ren Yuan and others to recruit them, fearing later trouble, so the army did not return at once.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omits Meng Zhixiang’s non-arrival and compresses 兩川新定 / 分出招集 into a misleading ‘pacified the hills’.

proposals.before: As Yan’gui was about to go he saw Empress Liu: “I heard from Yansi that affairs in Shu are already beyond remedy; disaster will strike in an instant—how can one go three thousand li back and forth for orders from the granary!”
proposals.after: As Yan’gui was about to go he saw Empress Liu: “I heard from Yansi that affairs in Shu are already beyond remedy; disaster will strike in an instant—how can one go three thousand li back and forth awaiting orders!”
proposals.reason: 廩命 is rendered as ‘orders from the granary,’ which is semantically opaque; the sense is awaiting/receiving orders over a long round trip.

proposals.before: Jiji had been castrated young and left no sons.
proposals.after: From youth Jiji suffered a eunuch-like affliction and left no sons.
proposals.reason: 病閹 denotes a disabling eunuch-like condition, not necessarily surgical castration; ‘castrated’ overstates the Chinese.

proposals.before: Hearing Chongtao might stay, Zhuangzong sent Xiang Yansi to hurry withdrawal.
proposals.after: Hearing that Chongtao wished to remain in Shu, Zhuangzong was also displeased and sent the eunuch Xiang Yansi to urge Jiji to withdraw the army.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic drops Zhuangzong’s displeasure, Xiang Yansi’s eunuch status, Jiji as addressee, and Shu.

decisions.reason: 神閔敬皇后 is the posthumous title Shenminjing; Jing Shenmin reverses the three title characters.
The literal field has the same reversed title; 神閔敬 must be Shenminjing.
韓氏為淑妃，伊氏為德妃 separately enfeoffs each woman; “Yi Defei” fuses person and title, while “Yi was made Defei” keeps the parallel.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 封韓氏為淑妃，伊氏為德妃

decisions.reason: 許州節度使 is Xu Prefecture (Xuchang), not 徐州; Xuzhou is a different place.
The literal likewise misreads 許州 as Xuzhou; Xu Prefecture matches the Chinese.
兩河 denotes the two He regions as a historical term, not the vague “Yellow River country.”
嗣肱 is Sìgōng; 肱 is gōng, so Sigu is a misreading.
The literal repeats the same misromanization of 嗣肱 as Sigu.
嗣肱 opens this unit; the subject must be Sigong, not Sigu.
Same 嗣肱→Sigong correction in the literal field.
嗣肱獲梁將 names Sigong as the capturer, not Sigu.
The literal likewise requires Sigong for 嗣肱.
蓚縣 is Tiao (not Zhuo), 嗣肱 is Sigong, and 蔚州 is Yu (not Wei); the proposed after corrects all three.
The literal has the same three errors—Zhuo/Sigu/Wei for 蓚/嗣肱/蔚—and the proposed after fixes them.
嗣肱取媯、儒、武 again requires Sigong, not Sigu.
Same Sigong correction for 嗣肱 in the literal field.
李可舉 is Li Keju; Li Keyong (李克用) is Taizu himself and cannot be the opponent named here.
Literal likewise needs Li Keju for 李可舉, and 雲、蔚 are Yun and Yu, not Yun and Wei.

decisions.after: Cunmei was Prince of Yong, Cunba Prince Yong, Cunli Prince of Xue, Cunwo Prince of Shen, Cunyi Prince of Mu, Cunque Prince of Tong, Cunji Prince of Ya.
decisions.reason: 邕王 and 永王 are distinct fiefs; the proposal’s Chinese parentheticals are disallowed in English, so split them as Prince of Yong (邕王, Cunmei) versus Prince Yong (永王, Cunba).

decisions.after: Cunmei was Prince of Yong, Cunba Prince Yong, Cunli Prince of Xue, Cunwo Prince of Shen, Cunyi Prince of Mu, Cunque Prince of Tong, Cunji Prince of Ya.
decisions.reason: Literal likewise collapses 邕王 and 永王; use English-only Prince of Yong versus Prince Yong without Chinese graphs.
叔父 and 季父 identify Kening as Zhuangzong’s younger uncle; the idiomatic omission loses that kinship, which the proposed after restores.
檢校太尉 is acting Grand Commandant; Grand Preceptor would be 太師.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 遷檢校太尉、同中書門下平章事

decisions.reason: The literal repeats the 太尉/太師 confusion; Grand Commandant is correct.
陛下 is His Majesty, 侍中 is Palace Attendant, and 衡、華 are Mount Heng and Mount Hua—not Father or Yi Yin and Huo Guang.
The literal’s Yi Yin and Huo Guang invent persons for 衡、華; Mount Heng and Mount Hua match the metaphor.
兩川新定、孟知祥未至、分出招集 are omitted or distorted in the compressed idiomatic; the proposed after restores those facts.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 兩川新定，孟知祥未至……分出招集

少病閹 is a eunuch-like affliction from youth, not proven surgical castration; the proposed wording matches the Chinese.
亦不悅、宦者、趣繼岌班師、留蜀 are all in the Chinese and missing from the compressed idiomatic; the after restores them.
